sources.title: Introducing Grok 4.7
sources.evidence: Dated September 21, 2026. Announces same-day availability through Cursor, Grok Build and Grok API; describes a new, larger base than Grok 4.6 and longer reinforcement learning on difficult tasks. Does not provide a numerical model size or network structure.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 model specification
sources.evidence: Exact public model payload identifies grok-4.7, TEXT/IMAGE input, TEXT output, maxPromptLength 500000, functionCalling=true and reasoning=true. Supported reasoning efforts are low, medium, high and xhigh, default high. No parameter count or architecture is present.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 Model Card, revision 2026-09-21
sources.evidence: Accessed all 30 pages. Pages 3–4 identify SpaceXAI as an xAI DBA and developer, describe text/image input and text output, hosted distribution, and pretraining followed by supplemental training, SFT and RL. Consumer surfaces were planned later. No parameter count, dense/MoE classification, or Transformer layout is disclosed.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 Model Card, earlier public file
sources.evidence: Accessed the earlier linked September 21 card and compared its introduction/training sections and full text against the current file. This version also omits total/active counts and network topology; it does not supply a missing numerical-size comparison table.

sources.title: Elon Musk original Grok 4.6 / Grok 4.7 scale post, July 28, 2026
sources.evidence: Official X syndication JSON confirms author elonmusk (user 44196397), timestamp 2026-07-28T15:20:02Z and post ID 2082123925283041545. The returned text explicitly describes the future Grok 4.7 as a 2.1T model, following Grok 4.6. It does not define total versus active parameters or confirm the final September checkpoint. Canonical post: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2082123925283041545. The returned post is truncated after its capability claims; the numerical disclosure is intact.

sources.title: API release notes: September 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Exact September 21 entry announces grok-4.7 availability on the xAI API with 500k context, text/image input, text output, and four reasoning efforts. Fast is expressly the same model on faster serving infrastructure, rather than another checkpoint.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 developer guide
sources.evidence: Lists the exact identifier, 500000-token context, text/image input and text output, function calling, web/X search and code execution. Specifies low/medium/high/xhigh effort, high default. Fast uses the same model and is restricted to product serving options.

sources.title: Reasoning: Grok 4.7 controls
sources.evidence: Names grok-4.7 specifically, lists effort controls, states that reasoning cannot be disabled, and describes encrypted reasoning returned by its Responses API.

sources.title: Files Overview
sources.evidence: Attaching a file activates attachment_search and creates an agentic document-search workflow. PDF handling through this interface is not evidence for native PDF input to the underlying model.

sources.title: Enterprise Terms of Service, updated August 14, 2026
sources.evidence: Sections 1.1 and 4.1 grant limited hosted-service/API access and retain ownership of underlying models and technology. Supports descriptive proprietary classification for the hosted model; no model-weight license is granted.

sources.title: Official xai-org public model inventory
sources.evidence: Accessed inventory contains xai-org/grok-1 and xai-org/grok-2, not Grok 4.7. Used with its documented hosted distribution and proprietary terms, not as standalone proof from search absence.

sources.title: Cursor Grok 4.7 model and training overview
sources.evidence: Explicitly says Cursor trained Grok 4.7 jointly with SpaceXAI on a new larger base than Grok 4.6, with longer reinforcement learning. Gives 256k standard and 500k long context for Cursor. Does not disclose numerical model size or dense/MoE structure.

sources.title: Grok 4.7: Cursor model help
sources.evidence: Calls it a first-party model jointly built with SpaceXAI. Describes a larger base and longer training, four reasoning effort levels, 256k standard and 500k long context. Does not state that it shares the Grok 4.5/4.6 base or disclose network topology.

sources.title: Elon Musk Grok 4.7 launch-day post, September 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Official X JSON confirms the founder post on September 21 at 16:25:47Z praises the released model, but contains no numerical model size or network-structure disclosure. Canonical post is https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2102071804495872374. Later exact-model founder/researcher searches did not locate a final-checkpoint count confirmation.

sources.title: Improved token efficiency for longer agent runs, September 23, 2026
sources.evidence: Later developer research covers agent-harness prompts, tool loading, caching, file-read compression and subagent usage; it does not disclose Grok 4.7 production parameter counts or network architecture.

sources.title: Mixture-of-Kittens: MoE training megakernel, August 4, 2026
sources.evidence: Developer research explicitly associates this production MoE kernel with Composer training. It does not identify Grok 4.7 as using that topology; do not transfer its MoE description to a different model.

name.note: Exact public product name and API identifier.

developer.note: The card expressly allows xAI and SpaceXAI interchangeably and identifies the developer; retain the established xAI catalog identity despite current SpaceXSI branding. Cursor separately confirms joint development; record this collaboration without changing the catalog developer key.

family.note: Named Grok release and successor to Grok 4.6.

release_date.note: Same-day primary API/product release announcement. Earlier founder roadmap dates were forecasts, not public availability; later provider listings do not replace this date.

open_weights.note: Documented hosted model, with proprietary service terms and no public Grok 4.7 checkpoint in the official weight inventory.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model under developer service terms, rather than an open-weight license identifier.

parameters_b.note: A directly accessed founder post announces Grok 4.7 as a 2.1T model before release. Preserve that nominal disclosure below; the statement does not define total versus active size, and the released model cards and launch documentation do not confirm a final checkpoint count. Do not label the number wholly undisclosed, or transfer Grok 4.6/4.20 counts. Cursor launch/help and the founder launch-day post also omit the final count; a larger new base is consistent with, but does not quantify, the announced 2100B.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact Grok 4.7 active-per-token count found in the reviewed primary materials or founder disclosure. Neither a nominal overall size nor a serving speed establishes active parameters.

architecture.note: The launch establishes a different, larger base than Grok 4.6; training descriptions do not establish dense/MoE routing, Transformer layout, layers, attention or experts. Targeted searches for exact-model developer training/interpretability research and original researcher posts found no further structural disclosure. Do not inherit Grok 4.5/4.6 topology. Cursor confirms a new larger base; its MoE kernel paper describes Composer, and its September 23 research concerns the harness rather than this model network.

context_window.note: Native xAI context limit, independently confirmed in the exact model payload. Cursor exposes a 256k standard product tier and 500k long context, consistent with retaining the native maximum.

modalities.note: Remove PDF from direct inputs: uploaded documents invoke attachment_search. Producing documents, images or code-executed artifacts through tools does not add native output modalities.

reasoning.note: Exact model supports low, medium, high and xhigh effort, defaults to high, and cannot disable reasoning.

tool_call.note: Exact model feature flag and developer guide establish function calling; server tools include web search, X search and code execution.

description.value: Grok reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work, with text and image input, text output and configurable reasoning effort.
description.note: Replace frontier-ranking language with documented purpose, modalities and configurable reasoning.

patch.notes: Released on the xAI API September 21, 2026. Native inputs are text and images; PDF attachments are searched through a tool. Reasoning supports low, medium, high (default) and xhigh and cannot be disabled. Elon Musk described the forthcoming Grok 4.7 as a 2.1T (2100B) model on July 28, 2026; this is an accessed primary founder disclosure, but neither released card defines its total/active count or confirms the final checkpoint size. Active parameters and network architecture remain undisclosed. Grok 4.7 Fast is the same model served faster, not another checkpoint. Cursor confirms joint development on a new larger base; its 256k standard product tier does not replace the native 500k maximum.

announced_parameter_count.basis: Founder-announced nominal size before release; total/active definition and final deployed checkpoint count not confirmed.

summary: Confirmed September 21 native release, 500k context, closed proprietary distribution, function calling and four mandatory reasoning-effort levels. Removed tool-mediated PDF from native modalities and replaced promotional description. Located and directly accessed the primary founder 2.1T announcement; retain it explicitly as an announced nominal size while final total and active counts remain unverified/undisclosed respectively. Both public model-card files omit network structure; no sibling counts or topology transferred.
